newsitem.title: BELGIUM: German official warns on need for EMU budget pact.
newsitem.headline: German official warns on need for EMU budget pact.

text.p: A senior German finance official on Wednesday warned that a credible budget stability pact for countries joining a single currency was essential and predicted one could be realised with further negotiations.
"There has to be an agreement on how to conduct this policy after monetary union," said Klaus Regling, director general of international financial and monetary issues at Germany's finance ministry.

Speaking to a conference on economic and monetary union (EMU), Regling said there would likely be an accord on a budget pact, but he was unsure whether all the details could be nailed down before a December EU summit in Dublin.
"We will try to do it by Dublin but if it's not possible I think it's not a disaster," he added.

"The most likely outcome is that we will have an agreement on the stability pact that is satisfactory, if not in Dublin, then in Amsterdam," he said, referring to the following scheduled EU summit next June.
Regling said about 90 percent of the issues on such a pact had been resolved, but the remaining 10 percent were important because they concerned potential loopholes.
"If one doesn't close the loopholes the agreement on the other 90 percent may not be worth very much," he said.
